It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1995.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=February 8, 2021}} The district consists of three [[barangay]]s in northeastern Makati: [[Guadalupe Nuevo]], Guadalupe Viejo, and Pinagkaisahan. The ten [[Embo, Taguig|Embo barangays]]—Cembo, Comembo, East Rembo, Pembo, Pitogo, [[Post Proper Northside]], [[Post Proper Southside]], Rizal, South Cembo and West Rembo—were formerly part of the district until 2023, when their jurisdiction was transferred from Makati to Taguig, following the resolution of the [[Makati–Taguig boundary dispute|territorial dispute between the two cities]].{{cite news|url=https://mb.com.ph/2023/4/3/taguig-lgu-lauds-sc-decision-over-fort-bonifacio-ownership|title=Taguig LGU lauds SC decision over Fort Bonifacio ownership|first=Jonathan|last=Hicap|date=April 3, 2023|work=Manila Bulletin|accessdate=July 17, 2023}}{{cite news |last=Caliwan |first=Christopher Lloyd |date=November 8, 2023 |title=DILG's Taguig office to take control of 10 EMBO villages |url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1213248 |work=Philippine News Agency |access-date=November 12, 2023}}{{cite news|url=https://www.rappler.com/philippines/elections/comelec-allows-embo-residents-taguig-vote-congressman-2025/|title=Comelec allows EMBO residents in Taguig to vote for congressman in 2025|date=September 27, 2024|accessdate=September 28, 2024|work=Rappler|first=Dwight|last=de Leon}} It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Alden Almario]] of [[Makatizens United Party]] (MKTZNU).{{cite web|url=https://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=February 8, 2021}} The district was created in 1995 when Makati was granted cityhood. However, its first representative-elect, [[Agapito Aquino]], was disqualified before he could take office that year due to lack of residency. There were no special elections held to fill vacancy. As a result, Makati was effectively represented by one representative until 1998. The fate of the second district is uncertain due to the Supreme Court ruling on the Makati–Taguig territorial dispute due to the remaining barangays not fulfilling the constitutional requirement of 250,000 residents. Makati could be reduced back to a [[Makati's at-large congressional district|single district]].{{cite news |last1=Aurelio |first1=Julie |title=SC ruling opens issue on Taguig House seats |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1805272/sc-ruling-opens-issue-on-taguig-house-seats |access-date=July 23, 2023 |work=Philippine Daily Inquirer |date=July 22, 2023 |language=en}} Pending legislation, the status quo of its existence, despite it being reduced to three barangays, is expected to prevail.{{cite news |title=After SC ruling, Makati's congressional seat hangs in the balance |url=https://www.rappler.com/newsbreak/in-depth/after-supreme-court-ruling-land-dispute-makati-congressional-seat-hangs-balance/ |access-date=July 27, 2023 |work=Rappler |date=July 26, 2023}} However, since [[2025 Philippine general election|2025]], voters from the Embo barangays do not vote for the representative of this district as they were reapportioned between the two existing districts of Taguig–Pateros.{{cite news|url=https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/2024/6/25/-embo-residents-can-t-vote-for-house-rep-in-2025-comelec-1401|title='Embo' residents can't vote for House rep in 2025: Comelec|first=Sherrie Ann|last=Torres|date=June 25, 2024|access-date=June 25, 2024|work=ABS-CBN News}} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Congress ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
